en.headline: Maritime and Aviation Training Fund commitment reaches HK$500 million
en.dek: Transport and Logistics Bureau secretary Mable Chan said the fund has supported more than 24,000 students and practitioners by September after successive top-ups.
body: The Maritime and Aviation Training Fund now carries a total commitment of HK$500 million, according to a blog post by Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan published on Saturday.

Ms Chan wrote that education and talent form the foundation of Hong Kong’s maritime and aviation industries. The fund, launched in 2014, has also drawn more than 140,000 attendances at industry-promotion events.

This year’s Policy Address places new emphasis on establishing a Hong Kong Maritime Academy and a school-enterprise collaboration model involving local and overseas institutes as well as major shipping companies. A school-based logistics curriculum introduced last year expanded this October into maritime studies through a dedicated resource centre offering teaching materials, talks and visits for primary and secondary pupils.

By August, professional programmes covering airport management, security and aviation services had recorded more than 450,000 attendances. The academy is examining specialised courses on the C919 aircraft with the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China and related maintenance organisations.

zh.headline: 海事及空運人才培訓基金承擔總額達五億港元
zh.dek: 運輸及物流局局長陳美寶表示，基金經多次注資後，截至九月已惠及超過二萬四千名學生及從業員。
body: 運輸及物流局局長陳美寶周六在網誌指出，海事及空運人才培訓基金的承擔總額現已達五億港元。
陳美寶表示，教育與人才是香港海運及航空業發展的基石。基金於二零一四年成立，至今亦吸引超過十四萬人次參與業界推廣活動。
今年施政報告重點推動成立香港海事學院，並推行「校企協作」模式，伙伴包括本地及海外知名海事院校與大型航運公司。去年三月推出的校本物流課程，今年十月透過海事專業教育資源中心擴展至海事學科，為中小學生提供教材、講座及實地參觀。
截至八月，涵蓋機場管理、保安及航空服務的專業課程累計出席人次超過四十五萬。學院正與中國商飛及相關維修機構研究開設C919專項課程，內容涵蓋飛行、維修及航空管理。
